questions.title: Papilloma is the benign epithelial tumour of non-glandular surfaces
questions.question: A benign epithelial cell neoplasm derived from non-glandular surfaces is referred to as:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Hamartoma is a disorganised overgrowth of tissue elements normal to the site, not the term for a benign neoplasm of non-glandular epithelium.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Squamous cell carcinoma is a malignant, not benign, epithelial tumour.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adenoma is the benign epithelial tumour of glandular, not non-glandular, surfaces.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sarcoma is a malignant mesenchymal tumour, not a benign epithelial one.
explanations.E: Correct. Papilloma is the benign epithelial cell neoplasm derived from non-glandular surfaces (such as skin or mucosal squamous epithelium), characteristically growing as multiple finger-like (papillary) projections. This distinguishes it from adenoma, the benign tumour of glandular epithelium, and from the malignant options (squamous cell carcinoma, sarcoma) and hamartoma, a developmental malformation rather than a true neoplasm.

questions.title: Adenoma is the benign tumour of glandular epithelium
questions.question: If a tumor is benign and glandular in origin, what is it called?

explanations.A: Correct. Adenoma is the term for a benign tumour of glandular epithelial origin, forming gland-like or duct-like structures resembling the tissue it arises from. This distinguishes it from papilloma (the benign tumour of non-glandular surfaces), carcinoma (a malignant epithelial tumour), a Krukenberg tumour (a specific metastatic, not primary benign, ovarian tumour) and the general descriptor "malignant."
explanations.B: Incorrect. A Krukenberg tumour is a metastatic (typically gastric-signet-ring-cell-derived) tumour of the ovary, not the general term for a benign glandular tumour.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Papilloma is the benign epithelial tumour of non-glandular, not glandular, surfaces.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Carcinoma denotes a malignant epithelial tumour, not a benign one.
explanations.E: Incorrect. "Malignant" is a behavioural descriptor, not the specific name for a benign glandular tumour.

questions.title: Papilloma characteristically shows finger-like projections
questions.question: Which of the following is a benign tumor of the epithelium characterized by multiple finger like projections?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fibroma is a benign mesenchymal (connective tissue) tumour, not an epithelial one, and does not characteristically show finger-like projections.
explanations.B: Correct. Papilloma is the benign epithelial tumour characterised grossly by multiple finger-like (papillary) projections growing outward from the epithelial surface. This distinctive gross morphology, alongside its non-glandular epithelial origin, is what distinguishes papilloma from fibroma, adenoma or lymphoma among the options.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adenoma, the benign tumour of glandular epithelium, typically forms gland-like structures rather than the finger-like papillary projections this stem describes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lymphoma is a malignant tumour of lymphoid tissue, not a benign epithelial tumour with a papillary morphology.
